_README: CMJ BETS — Claude Code permission policy (project / team-wide)
Goal: maximum autonomy on SAFE, reversible operations; an explicit
confirmation prompt only for IRREVERSIBLE or HIGH-RISK actions.
HOW RESOLUTION WORKS:
deny  >  ask  >  allow   (category wins regardless of source file).
Anything NOT matched by any rule falls through to defaultMode,
which is left at 'default' = prompt. So the safe posture is:
we ALLOW a tight set of known-safe commands, ASK for known-danger
commands, and everything unlisted prompts by default.
PATTERN LIMITATION (important):
Bash()/PowerShell() rules match a command by PREFIX with a single
trailing '*'. They cannot match text in the middle of a command.
Because every script run starts with the interpreter path
(venv\Scripts\python.exe ...), we can safely allow SPECIFIC named
scripts, but we CANNOT prefix-match an embedded SQL keyword or a
script name that appears after the interpreter. Consequences:
- Inline DB mutations (python -c "... DELETE/DROP/UPDATE/ALTER")
are deliberately NOT allowlisted, so they hit the default
prompt. Do not add a blanket 'python*' allow — it would defeat
this and auto-approve destructive one-liners.
- pull_odds.py (spends API budget) is likewise NOT allowlisted
and will prompt, while the free idempotent pulls are allowed.
File-path rules (Edit/Write) DO support full globs, so the .env /
data/ / scheduler-file gates below are exact.
AUTO-APPROVED (allow): tests, free idempotent data pulls, read-only
git, pip installs, pycache clearing, reads, edits under scripts/
and dashboard/.
GATED (ask): edits to .env, data/, the scheduler files; git push /
remote ops; Windows Task Scheduler (schtasks / *-ScheduledTask) and
powercfg. Plus, by default-prompt: inline SQL mutations, pull_odds.py,
and any system command not listed here.
